Subject (in full) Arrest of two political suspects by Sinza Station.

Made by....................and............................Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

x Localo 08079F/3(

At 7 a.m. July 7, 1939, detectives attached to
Sinza Station carried out a search of the Sinza Lodging
House, 841 Sinza Road, and took into custody two persons
named Tsang Dah Tien ( 張大天 ) and Li Chi Chong
( 李其昌 ) respectively, on suspicion that they were
engaged in political and subversive activities in
Shanghai. The two prisoners were brought to Head-
quarters the same morning and questioned by Special
Branch. A statement taken from Tsang Dah Tien is
attached hereto. Li Chi Chong was found to be a man
without political leanings and no statement, therefore,
was taken from him.

The two persons were returned to Sinza Station
at 5 p.m. on July 7th, 1939.

E.

1939年7月7日上午7时，隶属于新闸捕房的侦探搜查了位于新闸路841号的新闸旅社，并以涉嫌在上海从事政治及颠覆活动为由，拘留了两名分别名为张大天（Tsang Dah Tien）和李其昌（Li Chi Chong）的人。两名囚犯于同日上午被带至总局，由特务科进行讯问。附呈取自张大天的供词一份。李其昌经查无政治倾向，故未取其供词。

两人于1939年7月7日下午5时被送回新闸捕房。

我叫张大天（張大千），又名张应康（張應康），又名张仰之（張仰之）。现年40岁，江苏吴江人，居住于格罗西路（Route Grouchy）2号。

21岁时，我在吴江的中国体育专科学校完成学业，随后前往江阴县第六小学任教。23岁（1922年）时，我加入浙江省陆军第一师，担任士官，该师师长是我的亲戚潘国光（Pan Kuo Kwang）。

1924年，我成为上海防守司令公署的副官；1925年调任江西省政府任书记员；1926年重新入伍，追随时任浙江省政府主席的夏超（Hsia Tsao）；同年，夏超因发动反对浙江军阀孙传芳（Sung Chuan Fan）的叛乱失败而被斩首，我也随之离开军队；1927年，我被国民革命军暂编第十五师师长余宪文（Yu Shien Wen）雇用，在浙江招募士兵（此时上海已被国民革命军占领）。1927年晚些时候，我被任命为浦东周浦禁烟局局长；1928年调往常熟，担任该市警察分局局长；1929年被任命为苏州警察局督察长。1931年我从警察局辞职，此后大部分时间待在家乡

Wu Kong, owing to ill-health.
After the withdrawal of the Chinese troops from
Shanghai and Soochow in November, 1937, I went to Hangchow
and thence via Ningpo reached Shanghai on January 27, 1938.
Immediately on arriving here, I went to see Wong Ih Ping
( 王一平 ), a Manchurian, who occupied a room in the Denis
Apartment, B'well Road. He is at present in Peiping and
has close relations with the Japanese Intelligence Service.
He lost no time in bringing me to see Ohtsuki ( 大槻 ) at
the Palace Hotel. I knew Ohtsuki ( 大槻 ) in the Spring
of 1937. Ostensibly he is known as a reporter of the "Hochi
Shimbun" ( 报知新闻 ), a Japanese newspaper, but I
understand that he is also a secret service worker of the
Japanese Government. He can speak Chinese fluently and
has a comprehensive knowledge of the conditions prevailing
in Shanghai and China. He brought Wong Ih Ping and me to
see Major Donowaki ( 堂脇 ) at Banzaikwan, Minghong Road. I was told
by Major Donowaki that Lieutenant General Yanagawa ( 柳川 ),
his superior officer, had his headquarters established in
Hangchow. Numerous matters relating to the pacification
of the cities and towns in the Japanese occupied area had to
be arranged and the Japanese army required my service to
assist them in forming political or quasi-political organi-
zations to handle and expedite these affairs. He also told
me that I knew the gentry in the cities surrounding Hangchow
and requested me to use my influence to induce them to form
a quasi-military unit to maintain peace and order in their

吴江，因健康不佳。
1937年11月中国军队从上海和苏州撤退后，我前往杭州，随后经宁波于1938年1月27日抵达上海。抵达此处后，我立即去拜访了王一平（Wong Ih Ping），他是一名满洲人，住在倍开尔路（B'well Road）的德尼公寓（Denis Apartment）的一个房间里。他目前在北京，与日本情报机构关系密切。他随即带我去见大槻（Ohtsuki），地点在派拉蒙酒店（Palace Hotel）。我是1937年春天认识大槻（Ohtsuki）的。表面上他是日本报纸《报知新闻》（Hochi Shimbun）的记者，但我了解到他也是日本政府的特务人员。他能说流利的中文，对上海和中国的局势有全面的了解。他带着王一平和我去明宏路（Minghong Road）万岁馆（Banzaikwan）见堂脇（Donowaki）少佐。堂脇少佐告诉我，他的上级柳川（Yanagawa）中将已在杭州设立总部。有关日军占领区城镇的“治安肃正”事宜需作安排，日军需要我的服务，协助他们组建政治或准政治组织来处理并加速这些事务。他还告诉我，我认识杭州周边城市的士绅，请求我利用我的影响力促使他们组建一支准军事部队，以维持各自城市的和平与秩序。

respective cities. After some consideration I agreed to
accept his proposal. On January 28, I was given $200.00
by Major Donowaki to enable me to purchase some clothing.
He told me to meet Ohtsuki at Palace Hotel on the after-
noon of February 1, 1938. At 3 p.m. Feb. 1, 1938, I called
on Ohtsuki and we left for the New Asia Hotel, Tiendong Road,
by motor car. At dawn the following morning, Major Donowaki,
Ohtsuki, myself and a number of Japanese and Chinese, one
of whom was reported to be Chow Feng Chi (周鳳岐)
(Minister of War of the Reformed Government, assassinated on
7.3.38, outside 80 Avenue du Roi Albert), left in two
aeroplanes for Hangchow arriving there about one hour later.

At Hangchow I was interviewed by Inoue, and a major
general, name not known, who was the chief of staff of
divisions under Lieutenant Gen. Yanagawa. The same day I
was interviewed by Chow Feng Chi, then Chairman of the
Chekiang Provincial Government, sponsored by the Japanese.
They impressed upon me that for the welfare of the Chinese
people I should exert my best efforts to carry out the
mission to be assigned to me which I understood was to be
the pacification of the people.

On February 4, I, accompanied by Ohtsuki and four
Japanese military police, proceeded to Huchow, Nanzing,
Chingzah, Pingvong and Wu Kong along the Soochow-Kashing
highway
~~Railway line~~ in a motor car. We talked with the autonomous
committees formed by the gentry at these places, urging them
to advise those people who have deserted their homes and

在杭州，井上（Inoue）和一位姓名不详的少将（柳川中将麾下各师的参谋长）接见了我。同日，当时由日本人支持的浙江省政府主席周凤岐也接见了我。他们向我强调，为了中国人民的福祉，我应尽最大努力执行指派给我的任务，据我理解，该任务即是安抚民众。

2月4日，在大槻和四名日本宪兵的陪同下，我乘车沿苏嘉公路~~铁路线~~前往湖州、南京（原文如此，疑为嘉兴或其他地名之误，但依原文译）、青浦（原文拼写Chingzah，音译青扎，结合上下文应为青浦或附近地区）、平湖（Pingvong，音译平旺，疑为平湖）和吴江。我们与这些地方由士绅组成的自治委员会交谈，敦促他们劝告那些逃离家园和

farms to return, encouraging them to do their best to
revive business in their respective districts and persuad-
ing them to ask the people to surrender all arms to the
Japanese if they kept any. On February 7, we returned to
Hangchow and reported to the Japanese Military authorities
that we had been quite successful in our mission as the
autonomous committees of all the places we visited agreed
to take our advice.

On February 11, 1938, I, accompanied by Donowaki,
went to call at these places again. At each place he
introduced me to the commanders of the Japanese garrison
forces so that I could apply to them for assistance in
future in connection with my mission which was to cooperate
the Japanese Military in inducing, by means of monetary
payments, the Chinese guerillas and bandits to surrender
or by other measures.

On February 17, 1938, I returned to Hangchow with
Catsuki and Zee Poh Zung (徐樸誠), a relative of mine,
who was Chief of the Hangchow-Kashing-Huchow Salt-Smuggling
Preventive Corps of the National Government and had then
some 1,500 men, all armed under him.

He agreed with me to restore peace and order in these
places in cooperation with the Japanese for the welfare of
the people.

On Feb. 22, Zee Poh Zung and I came to Shanghai and
stayed in the China Hotel, Kweichow Road, of which Zee is a
shareholder. We visited the New Asia Hotel almost daily

1938年2月11日，我在堂脇的陪同下再次访问了这些地方。在每个地方，他都把我介绍给日本驻防部队指挥官，以便我今后在执行任务时能向他们寻求援助，我的任务是与日军合作，通过金钱收买或其他措施，诱使中国游击队和土匪投降。

1938年2月17日，我和大槻（原文Catsuki，疑为大槻Ohtsuki之误或另一日本人）以及我的亲戚徐樸誠（Zee Poh Zung）回到杭州，徐樸誠时任国民政府杭嘉湖缉私队队长，手下约有1500名全副武装的人员。

他同意与我合作，为了人民的福祉，与日本人一起恢复这些地方的和平与秩序。

2月22日，徐樸誠和我来到上海，住在贵州路的中国饭店，徐是该饭店的股东之一。我们几乎每天都去新亚酒店

to negotiate with the Special Service Section of the
Japanese Military regarding the formation of a "Pacification
Army". The eastern section of the New Asia Hotel was
allotted for the use of the preparatory office of the
"Pacification Army" of which I, Zee Poh Zung and Yang An
Shing (楊安心), a native of Tsingpu and formerly the
chief of the water police of that city, were the principal
promoters and Inoue, a follower of Col. Usuda, was the advisor.
On March 14, 1938, the Pacification Army was formally
inaugurated, and on March 18, Zee Poh Zung and I left for
Tsingzah, 12 li from Wu Kong, my native home, while Yang An
Shing went to Tsingpu. The three of us commenced to gather
together some ex-policemen and paotui members and armed them
with the weapons which we secured in the war area left by the
Chinese armies following their withdrawal.
Later, one Zee Foong Tsao (徐凤超) who was a native
of Zangshu, also joined us. By April, 1938, the Pacification
Army had its units distributed as follows:-

| District | Commander | No. of men | Monthly maintenance fee issued by the Japanese Military. |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1st District - Hangchow, Kashing, Sungkiang. | Zee Poh Zung | 2,000 | $40,000. |
| 2nd District - Soochow, Wusieh, Huchow. | Tsang Dah Tien | 2,000 | $24,000. |
| 3rd District - Shanghai, Tsingpu, Quinsan. | Yang An Shing | 2,500 | $18,000. |
| 4th District - Zangshu, Klangyin, Taichang. | Zee Foong Tsao | 600 | $12,000. |

There were 6 Japanese advisors in each of the 1st and
2nd districts and 4 in each of the 3rd and 4th districts, their
principal mission being to collect intelligence for

后来，一名叫徐凤超（Zee Foong Tsao）的常熟人也加入了我们。到1938年4月，绥靖军的部队分布如下：-

| 辖区 | 指挥官 | 人数 | 日军发放的每月维持费 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 第一辖区 - 杭州、嘉兴、松江。 | 徐樸誠 | 2,000 | $40,000. |
| 第二辖区 - 苏州、无锡、湖州。 | 张大天 | 2,000 | $24,000. |
| 第三辖区 - 上海、青浦、昆山。 | 杨安心 | 2,500 | $18,000. |
| 第四辖区 - 常熟、江阴、太仓。 | 徐凤超 | 600 | $12,000. |

the information of the Special Service Section of the
Japanese Military.

In name the 'Pacification army" were under the control
of the Pacification Headquarters of the Reformed Government
with one Ning Yuan Dao 任 伪 道 in charge but actually they were
subject to the orders of the Japanese Military. All the
villages which are some distance away from the railways or
high-ways in the Japanese occupied area were guarded by the
pacification army as the Japanese had confined themselves to
the large cities and never ventured to go beyond them.
The commanders of the pacification army visited Shanghai twice
then established in Shanghai
a month to receive instructions from the Headquarters.

In August, 1938, some 1,000 of the men under me at
Tsingzah were beseiged by the guerillas and they later
surrendered. I was myself present in Tsingzah at the time
but managed to escape with the assistance of a band of body-
guards.

In September, 1938, the remaining 1,000 men under me
in Soochow were disbanded by the Japanese troops on the ground
that they had not carried out their duty to the satisfaction
of the Japanese and in consequence I returned to Shanghai and
stayed in New Asia Hotel.

In October, 1938, I went to stay with my family at No.2
Route Grouchy. Since that time, I was appointed Councillor of
the Pacification Headquarters. I receive a pay of $320.00 per
mensem without the necessity of attending to any work.
This treatment was specially meted out by the Japanese because

名义上，“绥靖军”受维新政府绥靖总司令部控制，由任伪道（Ning Yuan Dao，音译，原文如此）负责，但实际上他们受命于日军。日军占领区内远离铁路或公路的所有村庄均由绥靖军守卫，因为日军只局限于大城市，从不冒险越出城市范围。绥靖军指挥官当时每月两次前往上海设立的总部接受指令。

1938年8月，我在青浦（原文Tsingzah）手下的约1000人被游击队包围，随后投降。当时我本人在青浦，但在保镖的帮助下得以逃脱。

1938年9月，我在苏州剩余的1000人被日军解散，理由是他们未能令日军满意地履行职责，因此我返回上海，住在新亚酒店。

1938年10月，我搬去与家人同住，地址是格罗西路2号。自那时起，我被任命为绥靖总司令部参议。我每月领取320美元薪水，无需处理任何工作。这种待遇是日本人特别给予的，因为

                                                                at present
            The Pacification Headquarters is/in Nanking.
Immediately after I was ousted from my post as commander of
the 2nd district of the pacification army, I learned that
one Chung Kuo Liang, (褚國良), ex-Divisional Officer of
the Kiangsu Water Police, was appointed to succeed me.
            Col. Usuda, who is at present in Kaifeng, serving as
chief of the Special Service Section there, recently addressed
me requesting me to proceed to work under him. As I am
unemployed meantime, I am considering acceding to his request.
            I have not participated in any activities in Shanghai
since I retired from active service in the Pacification Army.
I used to have my letters and communications received through
a friend named Nyi Ching Sz (倪竟時) living at Room 235,
214 Ningpo Road, owing to the fact that I, being known as a
traitor in Chinese circles, wish so to keep my address secret
in order to avoid any untoward incidents.
            I left my home, No.2 Route Grouchy for Ningpo Road at
about 10 p.m. July 6, together with Li Chi Chong (李其昌), my relative,
arriving there at about 10.30 p.m.
            My friend Nyi was not at home and I together with Li
Chi Chong went to Sinza Road to have some food at Yah Shing
Food Shop, Carter Road. It was then about 11.30 p.m. When
on my way home later in the evening, I saw the French Police
conduct strict searches of pedestrians who entered the French
Concession from the Settlement.    The finding of a Japanese

            绥靖司令部位于/在南京。
在我被免去绥靖军第二区司令的职务后，我随即得知，前江苏水上警察分局局长褚國良（Chung Kuo Liang）被任命接替我的职位。
            目前在开封担任特务科科长的臼田大佐（Col. Usuda），最近致信给我，要求我前去为他工作。由于我目前失业，我正在考虑接受他的请求。
            自从我从绥靖军退役以来，我没有参与过在上海的任何活动。过去，我的信件和通讯都是通过一位名叫倪竟時（Nyi Ching Sz）的朋友转交的，他住在宁波路214号235室，这是因为我在华人圈子中被视为汉奸，希望以此保密我的地址，以避免发生任何不测事件。
            7月6日晚上10点左右，我和我的亲戚李其昌（Li Chi Chong）一起离开格罗西路（Route Grouchy）2号的住所前往宁波路，大约在晚上10点30分到达那里。
            我的朋友倪先生不在家，我和李其昌便去静安寺路（Sinza Road）的卡德路（Carter Road）亚兴食品店（Yah Shing Food Shop）吃东西。当时大约是晚上11点30分。当晚稍后在我回家的路上，我看到法国警察对从租界进入法租界的行人进行严格搜查。如果他们发现我身上带有日本

人通行证，可能会给我自己带来不必要的麻烦，因此，我决定当晚不回家，而是去新闸旅馆（Sinza Lodging House）开一个房间。
1939年7月7日
早上7点左右，一支警察搜查队来到新闸旅馆，我因涉嫌在租界从事颠覆活动而被拘留。
1938年6月，我曾试图诱劝黄景山（Wong Ching San）加入绥靖军，但未成功。当时黄在浦东约有700人。

（批注：C 10/7）

（批：Please see if this file refers only to relative arrests the previous day & is of no interest to Special Branch. J.）

Misc. 319/39
2

"B"
Sinza
8th July,
39.

suspects arrested by search Parties.

Between 5 a.m. 7/7/39 and 1.30 a.m. 8/7/39,
search parties operating in Sinza District arrested on
various Roads and in various Lodging Houses and teashops,
a total of 22 male Chinese and one female Chinese.

All were finger printed and only 3 were found to
have criminal records and these were for minor offences
and of little or no importance.

Two male Chinese Tsang Dah Tien ( 張大天 ), age 40,
Soochow, and Li Kyih Chong ( 李其昌 ), age 42, Soochow,
u/Unemployed who were arrested at Room 323 Sinza Lodging
House, Sinza Road at 6.40 p.m. 7/7/39.

During interrogation of these two it was revealed
that the 1st named claimed to be an official of the
Reformed Government, Nanking, and was receiving a wage
of $320.00 per month and his presence in Shanghai
appeared to be of a political nature.

The 2nd named claimed to be a friend of the 1st
named stating they resided together in F/Concession.
Their separate versions of their movements on the
evening of 6/7/39 differed. Special Branch were there-
fore communicated with and on their instructions these
two were taken to Special Branch at 10 a.m. 7/7/39 for
interrogation.

（左侧手写批注：S.I. / D.S.R. / 11/7）

杂项 319/39
2

“B”
新闸
7月8日，
39年。

被搜查队逮捕的嫌疑人。

在1939年7月7日凌晨5点至1939年7月8日凌晨1点30分之间，在新闸区行动的搜查队在各种道路、旅馆和茶馆共逮捕了22名中国男性和1名中国女性。

所有人都按了指纹，只有3人发现有犯罪记录，且均为轻微罪行，重要性不大或毫无重要性。

两名中国男性，张大天（Tsang Dah Tien），40岁，苏州人，和李其昌（Li Kyih Chong），42岁，苏州人，无业，于1939年7月7日下午6点40分在新闸路新闸旅馆323室被捕。

在对这两人的审讯中透露，前者声称是南京维新政府的官员，月薪320.00美元，他在上海的出现似乎具有政治性质。

后者声称是前者的朋友，并称他们共同居住在法租界。两人关于1939年7月6日晚上的行踪说法不一。因此与特别支部取得联系，并根据其指示，这两人于1939年7月7日上午10点被带往特别支部接受审讯。

（左侧手写批注：S.I. / D.S.R. / 11/7）

pages.en:
Misc. 319/39          Kinza

" (Sheet 2)

At 4.10 p.m. /    , Lt. Capt. Crawford informed
the undersigned briefly of the result of their inter-
rogation and stated that Mr. Robertson, Officer i/c
Special Branch was of the opinion that there was no
point in holding these men. This information was passed
to A.D. "B" who instructed that they be released.

The two men were transported from Special Branch
to Kinza Station at 4.10 p.m. and were released from
this station at 6.1. p.m. 7/7/39.

A copy of statement taken by Special Branch will
be sent to this station on completion of translation.

                                D. S. I.

Sen.Det.i/c.
pages.zh:
杂项 319/39          静安寺

“（第2页）

下午4点10分，克劳福德上尉（Lt. Capt. Crawford）向本人简要通报了审讯结果，并表示特别支部主管罗伯逊先生（Mr. Robertson）认为扣留这些人没有意义。此信息已转告“B”区助理总监（A.D. "B"），他指示释放他们。

这两人于下午4点10分从特别支部被转运至静安寺捕房，并于1939年7月7日下午6点01分从该捕房获释。

特别支部所作供词的副本将在翻译完成后发送至本捕房。

                                D. S. I.

高级侦探主管
